analysis: No regression found; this change affects local operator guidance only. ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.swift head 44-58 factors out liveDecision, which keeps the process, coordinator, finite-time, written-age, startedAt, online and protocol==1 checks. currentStatus (head 10-22) still requires now-receivedAt<=snapshotMaxAge, so the strict removal decision is unchanged from base 18. displayedStatus (head 28-40) accepts an older receivedAt only while hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization(now) holds. It is display-only. summary (head 68-100) gives positive removal advice only when removalAuthorization == authorization and removalReady(removalAuthorization) (head 81-85). Otherwise it tells the user to keep profiles, preserving the TB-011 rule that removal needs a fresh current decision. DoctorRunner.swift head 34-35 derives both values from one snapshot and one `now`; head 75-76 passes the strict value. Residual effect: a delayed revocation could leave doctor showing "App Attest authorizes this connection" until expires_at. That would also skip AttestationReadiness and MDM hints (base 64, 105, gated by appAttestAuthorized). Per TB-002 and TB-011, local doctor verdicts are not trust evidence, and the coordinator authorizes every handoff (authorizeInferenceHandoff), so serving permission is unaffected. The doc lines head 92-107 match the code. Integration questions, since callers were not supplied: confirm that the status command and unenroll's KeepServing migration paths call currentProviderAuthorization/currentStatus for removal, not displayedProviderAuthorization. Also confirm that every summary caller passes the strict removalAuthorization rather than reusing the displayed value. Passing the displayed value as removalAuthorization would let a stale removal-ready lease yield positive removal advice (T-057). unenroll's own pre- and post-inspection readiness checks would still gate actual removal.
